Title: The auditory neurobiology of marsupials: a review.
Outcome: auditory system structure; auditory development; hearing
Evidence_Quote: In this review the structure of the auditory systems of the handful of marsupials which have been studied is described, the course of auditory development mapped, and the behavioral and electrophysiological manifestations of hearing examined.

Title: Mapping the perceptual magnet effect for speech using signal detection theory and multidimensional scaling.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: perception; discrimination; category goodness
Evidence_Quote: Experiment 1 collected goodness and identification judgments for 13 variants of the vowel /i/.

Title: Coherence analysis of envelope-following responses (EFRs) and frequency-following responses (FFRs) in infants and adults.
Outcome: EFR/FFR coherence growth and thresholds compared between infants and adults
Evidence_Quote: 'Best frequency' (i.e., infant 80 Hz and adult 40 Hz) EFR thresholds were the same for infants and adults at 500 and 1000 Hz, but infant EFR thresholds were poorer than adult thresholds at 2000 Hz.

Title: Estimating the contribution of non-sensory factors to infant-adult differences in behavioral thresholds.
Target_Age: infants 8 to 11 months old and adults
Stimulus_Type: 1 kHz tone in quiet and in masking noise (behavioral thresholds)
Outcome: Infant-adult threshold difference 12 dB; minimum masking level difference 8 dB
Evidence_Quote: In this investigation, thresholds in quiet and in increasing levels of a masking noise for a 1 kHz tone, in infants 8 to 11 months old and in adults, were determined.

Title: Fetal behaviour in normal and compromised fetuses. An overview.
Outcome: fetal motility; heart rate; hemodynamics; metabolism; response to stimulation; behavioural states
Evidence_Quote: Fetal intrauterine behaviour is not a stable situation but a continuous alternation of states characterized by significant changes in fetal motility, heart rate, hemodynamics, metabolism and response to stimulation.

Title: Spontaneous otoacoustic emissions in preterm neonates: prevalence and gender effects.
Target_Age: preterm neonates, from 30 to 40 weeks of conceptional age
Outcome: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions; prevalence; gender effects
Evidence_Quote: SOAEs were studied in more detail in 81 preterm neonates, from 30 to 40 weeks of conceptional age

Title: The postnatal development of frequency-place code and tuning characteristics in the auditory midbrain of the phyllostomid bat, Carollia perspicillata.
Target_Age: newborn and developing Carollia perspicillata bats
Stimulus_Type: Acoustic stimulation (characteristic-frequency mapping in inferior colliculus)
Outcome: Hearing range and tonotopy development in the inferior colliculus
Evidence_Quote: The experimental animal, Carollia perspicillata, has an adult hearing range of 7-110 kHz (characteristic frequencies) but lack any significant overrepresentation of a limited frequency band as known for rhinolophoid bats and Pteronotus. The audiogram of the newborn Carollia includes characteristic frequencies from 8 to 76 kHz, which is about 65% of the adult hearing range. As in adults, low frequencies are represented in the dorsolateral portion of the IC. However, at birth the ventromedial IC is non-responsive to acoustic stimulation up to intensities of 90 dB SPL.

Title: Responses of peripheral auditory neurons to two-tone stimuli during development: III. Rate facilitation.
Outcome: peripheral auditory neuron responses; rate facilitation
Evidence_Quote: some neural responses were facilitated under conditions of two-tone stimulation during the final stages of cochlear differentiation

Title: The relationship between auditory brainstem response latencies and behavioral thresholds in normal hearing infants and adults.
Stimulus_Type: Tone pips (ABR latencies and behavioral thresholds)
Outcome: ABR latency-behavioral threshold relationship by age group
Evidence_Quote: The relationship between behavioral thresholds and auditory brainstem response (ABR) latencies for 4 and 8 kHz tone pips were examined in normal-hearing 3-month-olds, 6-month-olds and adults.

Title: First appearance and development of electromotility in neonatal gerbil outer hair cells.
Target_Age: postnatal gerbils, ranging in age from 6 to 19 days
Outcome: electromotility; length changes in outer hair cells
Evidence_Quote: outer hair cells (OHCs) from apical and basal turns of the cochleae of postnatal gerbils, ranging in age from 6 to 19 days, were isolated and drawn into a glass microchamber

Title: Changes in the cat cochlear nucleus following neonatal deafening and chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation.
Stimulus_Type: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation; ABR/FFR testing
Outcome: Cochlear nucleus volume, spherical cell size and density after deafening/stimulation
Evidence_Quote: Profound hearing loss was confirmed in each animal by auditory brainstem response (ABR) and frequency following response (500 Hz) testing. Five of the kittens were implanted unilaterally with a scala tympani electrode array at ages 8-16 weeks. These kittens were stimulated daily for four hours at 2 dB above the evoked ABR threshold, over a period of three months, and subsequently euthanized for histological analysis at 26-32 weeks of age.

Title: Human fetal auditory threshold improvement during maternal oxygen respiration.
Outcome: fetal auditory threshold; fetal movement response
Evidence_Quote: estimating the threshold of the fetus to vibrio-acoustic stimulation applied to the maternal abdomen

Title: Pressure transfer function and absorption cross section from the diffuse field to the human infant ear canal.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: Diffuse-field pink noise from loudspeaker in reverberant room (ear-canal pressure measurement)
Outcome: Diffuse-field pressure transfer function and absorption cross section vs age
Evidence_Quote: The diffuse-field pressure transfer function from a reverberant field to the ear canal of human infants, ages 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months, has been measured from 125-10700 Hz.

Title: Longitudinal measurements of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions in infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America

Evidence_Quote: infants from this original group of 1-month-olds were tested at ages 3, 6, 12, and 24 months

Title: Improvement in sensorineural auditory threshold of the guinea-pig fetus following delivery.
Outcome: Neonatal ABR threshold on average 20 dB better than fetal threshold
Evidence_Quote: This was tested in this study by recording ABR thresholds to bone conducted stimuli in fetal guinea-pigs that were near full term and again in the same animals, after delivery and consequent pulmonary oxygenation.

Title: Do infants perceive word boundaries? An empirical study of the bootstrapping of lexical acquisition.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: discrimination of word boundary; non-nutritive sucking
Evidence_Quote: Three-day-old infants were tested with a non-nutritive sucking paradigm

Title: Recovery of auditory function and structure in the chick after two intense pure tone exposures.
Target_Age: neonatal chicks (exposed at 2 or 16 days of age)
Outcome: Threshold shift (about 57 dB at 0 days) and cochlear structural recovery after exposure
Evidence_Quote: Groups of neonatal chicks were examined in three experimental conditions that differed in the age and number of times they were exposed to a pure tone of 0.9 kHz at 120 dB SPL for 48 h. Several animals were exposed once at 2 or 16 days of age, while others were subjected twice to the above stimulus, first at 2 days and then at 16 days. Evoked potential measures of threshold shift, obtained at 0, 12 or 26 days post-exposure, were used to determine the degree of hearing loss and recovery. The average threshold loss in the mid-range frequencies was about 57 dB at 0 days for all three conditions.

Title: Aspects of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions in healthy newborns.
Stimulus_Type: Spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs) recorded in ear canal (no applied stimulus)
Outcome: SOAE prevalence 78%; levels -2 to 42 dB SPL; most emissions above 2 kHz
Evidence_Quote: The SOAE levels were between -2 and 42 dB SPL. The mean level per emitting ear was 8.0 dB SPL and not significantly different between right and left ears or genders.

Title: The growth of hearing loss in neonatal chicks exposed to intense pure tones.
Stimulus_Type: Intense pure tone exposure; probe tones for tuning curves
Outcome: Threshold shift and tuning sharpness vs exposure duration
Evidence_Quote: One-day-old chicks were exposed to an intense pure tone (0.9 kHz, 120 dB SPL) and assigned to one of eight groups based on continuous exposure durations from 1 to 200 h. As each animal was removed from the exposure, it was anesthetized and an electrode was placed in the nucleus magnocellularis. Sound-evoked potentials were used to measure absolute thresholds and frequency selectivity. Thresholds were measured at 10 frequencies between 0.1 and 4.5 kHz while frequency selectivity was assessed by a simultaneous masking tuning-curve procedure at five probe-tone frequencies between 0.3 and 2.5 kHz. Threshold shift was greatest at 1.3 kHz and reached a maximum loss of approximately 57 dB between 48 and 200 h of exposure.

Title: Simultaneous masking in newborn chickens.
Stimulus_Type: Tone masker and signal tones (simultaneous masking)
Outcome: Masking patterns mature at hatching, similar to adult humans
Evidence_Quote: In the first experiment data were collected with a 500-Hz masker presented at 15 or 25 dB above absolute threshold.

Title: The relation between head size and auditory brain-stem response interpeak latency maturation.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: auditory brain-stem response interpeak latency; head circumference
Evidence_Quote: particularly among preterm infants
